Definition: from G4314 and G2875; to strike at, i.e. surge against (as water); specially, to stub on, i.e. trip up (literally or figuratively):--beat upon, dash, stumble (at).
BiblicalUsage: Proskopto means to strike against, to stumble, to trip up. Jesus says, If any man walk in the day, he stumbleth not, because he seeth the light of this world. Israel stumbled because they sought it not by faith, and the disobedient stumble at the word. The devil quoted the promise that the angels would bear the Son up, lest at any time He dash His foot against a stone.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe stumbling is a question of light: the man who walks in the day does not stumble, and the man who walks by works instead of faith trips over the very Stone that was laid to save him. I hold that the devil's misuse of the promise proves the point, because he offered a verse and left out the walking.
